books.title: An Outline Grammar and Dictionary of the Kachari (Dimasa) Language
books.author: W. C. M. Dundas (based on Mani Charan Barman)
books.publisher: Eastern Bengal and Assam Secretariat Press
books.description: Historical grammatical monograph containing declension paradigms, conjugation outlines, and bilingual vocabulary lists.

pages.title: Grammatical Sketch Overview
pages.content: Dimasa Kachari represents a prominent speech variety of the Bodo-Garo linguistic group, spoken historically in North Cachar and surrounding hill tracts. Nouns do not exhibit grammatical gender inflections. Pluralization of human referents utilizes suffixes such as -rao. Morphological cases attach postpositionally to nominal stems.

pages.title: Nominal Inflection System
pages.content: Case relations in Dimasa are expressed via postpositions: Nominative is zero-marked; Accusative takes -ke or -khe on definite objects; Genitive takes -ni; Dative takes -ne or -thane; Locative is marked by -ha; Ablative is indicated by -niphang.

pages.title: Verbal Suffixation and Tense-Aspect
pages.content: Predicates in Dimasa remain invariant for person and gender. Aspect and temporal relations attach sequentially to the verbal stem: present imperfective -du, past -ba, future prospective -ma, imperative -bo, and negative prohibitive prefix da-.

pages.title: Numeral Classifiers Outline
pages.content: Counting expressions require sortal classifiers: human referents take sao-, non-human animates take ma-, cylindrical rigid objects take gon-, botanical plants take phang-. Numerals one through ten follow the sequence masi to maji.

books.title: Linguistic Survey of India: Volume III, Part II - Dimasa Section
books.author: Sir George Abraham Grierson
books.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing
books.description: Linguistic classification survey of Dimasa within the Bodo-Garo subgrouping of the Tibeto-Burman family.

pages.title: Genealogical Classification
pages.content: Dimasa is catalogued under the Bodo group of the Tibeto-Burman language family. It maintains close structural affinities with Boro, Garo, and Kokborok, while preserving archaic phonotactic features.

pages.title: Morphological Observations
pages.content: Syntactic analysis reveals SOV basic word order, extensive postpositional chaining, monosyllabic lexical roots, and numeral classifier constructions indicating definiteness based on constituent ordering.

pages.title: Comparative Lexical Notes
pages.content: Comparative analysis demonstrates regular sound correspondences across Sal languages, including conserved root vowels and cognate case affixes across the Bodo branch.

books.title: Dimasa Oral Traditions and Folklore Compendium
books.author: Tezpur University CEL & Dimasa Sahitya Sabha
books.publisher: Tezpur University Centre for Endangered Languages
books.description: Preserved oral literature, clan genealogical lore, and festival traditions documented with community scholars.

pages.title: Creation Lore and Ancestral Confluence
pages.content: Dimasa oral traditions record the ancestral origin at the sacred river confluence known as Sangsari Dingra, commemorating ancestral lineages and the cultural reverence for mountains and water bodies.

pages.title: The Post-Harvest Bushu Festival
pages.content: Bushu Dima is observed annually following the harvest of the winter rice crops. Celebrations include community gatherings, thanksgiving prayers to Creator Sibarai, traditional Baidima dances, and Khram drum rhythms.

pages.title: Historical Capitals and Archaeological Sites
pages.content: Oral history commemorates historical administrative seats including the ancient monolith structures of Dimapur, the rock-hewn temple architectures of Maibang, and the heritage monuments of Khaspur.
